feedback: If the learner asserts a conclusion without evidence, ask which specific measurement supports it before accepting it.
If the learner treats a very deep print as proof of running, note that depth may reflect ground softness or weight, while running is inferred from long stride relative to size.
Reward answers that acknowledge uncertainty and name an alternative explanation.
activities.intendedInsight: Justifying each reading out loud and handling novel tracks strengthens the habit of treating conclusions as tentative, evidence-based inferences.
learnerActions: Present your reading of a trackway and answer probing questions such as 'How do you know it was running?' and 'Could parallel tracks mean something other than a herd?'

Work through novel cases aloud: if two trackways cross, reason about which dinosaur passed first; compare what very deep prints versus shallow prints in the same ground might tell you; decide whether a small dinosaur could ever leave widely spaced prints and when.
Revise a claim when you cannot justify it, distinguishing a well-supported inference from a guess.
activities.title: Explain-your-thinking with a curious expert

feedback: If the learner judges speed from print size or depth, redirect them to stride length relative to print size.
Encourage the learner to name at least one alternative explanation before settling on a herd or chase reading.
activities.intendedInsight: The same measure→infer reasoning (size→body, stride→gait, pattern→behaviour) applies when tracks are examined in a three-dimensional, in-situ setting.
learnerActions: Move through a preserved three-dimensional trackway and locate a continuous line of prints.
Measure a print's size and the stride between prints in place, reading an approximate, tentative body size from the print and gait from the stride relative to size.
Interpret whether nearby parallel or converging trackways might suggest a group or a chase, framing each as a possible inference and naming an alternative.
Compare how examining tracks in a 3D setting feels against reading them on a flat bench.
activities.title: Explore a 3D trackway site in situ (alternative)
